Decidable (p : Prop) : TypeA `Bool` (that is, `decide p`) paired with a proof of `p` if `decide p` is `true` or a proof of `¬p` if `decide p` is `false`. The easiest way to extract these proofs is to use `of_decide_eq_true` or `of_decide_eq_false`. `Decidable` instances are primarily used via `if`-expressions and the tactic `decide`. In conditional expressions, the `Decidable` instance for the proposition is used to select a branch. In proofs, the tactic `decide` synthesizes an instance of `Decidable p`, attempts to reduce `decide p` to `true`, and then succeeds with the proof `of_decide_eq_true rfl` if it can. Because `Decidable` carries data, when writing `@[simp]` lemmas which include a `Decidable` instance on the LHS, it is best to use `{_ : Decidable p}` rather than `[Decidable p]` so that non-canonical instances can be found via unification rather than instance synthesis.
